items.title: Abdomen Narrative Laparoscopy
items.description: Minimally invasive endoscopic examination of the abdominal cavity using a laparoscope for direct visualization of intra-abdominal organs.
items.usage: Used to directly evaluate unexplained abdominal pain, infertility, suspected intra-abdominal pathology, adhesions, endometriosis, and staging of malignancies.

items.title: AXR AP
items.description: Plain radiographic examination of the abdomen obtained in the anteroposterior projection to evaluate bowel gas pattern and abdominal pathology.
items.usage: Used for rapid assessment of bowel obstruction or ileus, constipation, abnormal gas patterns, abdominal calcifications, foreign bodies, and position of tubes or devices.

items.title: AXR ERECT
items.description: Plain radiographic examination of the abdomen obtained in the erect position to evaluate air–fluid levels and free intraperitoneal air.
items.usage: Used to detect intestinal obstruction, paralytic ileus, and indirect signs of gastrointestinal perforation by demonstrating air–fluid levels and subdiaphragmatic free air.

items.title: AXR ERECT/SUPINE
items.description: Plain radiograph of the abdomen in both erect and supine positions to assess abdominal organs, bowel gas patterns, and free intraperitoneal air
items.usage: Used to evaluate the abdomen for bowel obstruction, air-fluid levels, free air under the diaphragm, or other gastrointestinal pathology.

items.title: AXR LAT
items.description: Plain radiographic examination of the abdomen obtained in the lateral projection to complement AP imaging and assess air–fluid levels and free intraperitoneal air.
items.usage: Used to improve detection of air–fluid levels, bowel obstruction, ileus, retroperitoneal pathology, and indirect signs of gastrointestinal perforation when AP view is inconclusive.

code.display: Plain X-ray of abdomen, lateral decubitus

items.title: AXR SUPINE
items.description: Plain radiographic examination of the abdomen obtained in the supine position to evaluate bowel gas distribution and abdominal soft-tissue outlines.
items.usage: Used to assess bowel dilatation, obstruction or ileus, fecal loading, abnormal gas patterns, abdominal calcifications, foreign bodies, and device positioning.

items.title: AXR-AP/LAT
items.description: Plain radiographic examination of the abdomen obtained in anteroposterior and lateral projections to assess bowel gas pattern and abdominal pathology.
items.usage: Used to evaluate bowel obstruction, ileus, perforation (indirect signs), constipation, abdominal calcifications, foreign bodies, and tube or device position.

items.title: BRONCHOGRAPHY
items.description: A diagnostic contrast imaging procedure in which contrast medium is introduced into the bronchial tree to visualize bronchial anatomy for evaluation of structural abnormalities.
items.usage: Primarily used to assess bronchial dilatation, strictures, congenital anomalies, or chronic airway pathology when detailed bronchial mapping is required.

items.title: C T SCAN FOOT
items.description: Computed tomography of the foot performed to obtain high-resolution cross-sectional evaluation of the tarsal, metatarsal, and phalangeal bones and adjacent joints.
items.usage: Used to assess complex or occult foot fractures, intra-articular involvement (e.g., calcaneus, talus), alignment abnormalities, bony lesions, and for pre-operative orthopedic planning when radiographs are inconclusive.

items.title: C.T SCAN BRAIN
items.description: A diagnostic imaging procedure using computed tomography to generate cross-sectional images of the brain for evaluation of intracranial anatomy and pathology.
items.usage: Used to rapidly assess intracranial conditions such as hemorrhage, infarction, mass lesions, edema, trauma, or hydrocephalus.

items.title: C.T SCAN LT.ELBOW JOINT
items.description: Computed tomography imaging of the left elbow joint performed for diagnostic evaluation of osseous and joint structures
items.usage: To evaluate the left elbow joint for fractures, degenerative changes, or other structural pathology using computed tomography.

items.title: C.T SCAN Triphasic
items.description: Triphasic CT scan performed in multiple contrast phases for detailed vascular and organ evaluation.
items.usage: Commonly used for liver, abdominal masses, tumors, and vascular assessment.

items.title: C.T SCAN W/S
items.description: Whole Spine CT Scan.
items.usage: Used to assess spinal trauma, fractures, deformities, disc disease, or spinal lesions.

items.title: C.T.SCAN BIL SCAPULA
items.description: Computed tomography of both scapulae performed to provide high-resolution cross-sectional evaluation of the scapular bones and adjacent shoulder girdle structures.
items.usage: Used to detect and characterize scapular fractures, bony lesions, deformities, post-traumatic alignment, and complex shoulder girdle pathology with superior anatomical detail.

items.title: C.T.SCAN HEAD
items.description: Computed tomography imaging of the head to evaluate intracranial and cranial structures for hemorrhage, infarction, mass lesions, trauma, or other acute or chronic abnormalities.
items.usage: Used to rapidly detect intracranial hemorrhage, ischemic stroke, space-occupying lesions, skull fractures, and other causes of acute neurological deficit.

items.title: C.T.SCAN L.S.SPINE
items.description: Spiral computed tomography of the lumbosacral spine performed to obtain high-resolution cross-sectional images of vertebrae, intervertebral discs, spinal canal, and adjacent structures.
items.usage: Used to evaluate lumbar spine trauma, degenerative disc disease, spinal canal stenosis, spondylolisthesis, fractures, infections, and bony causes of low back pain or radiculopathy.

items.description: Contrast angiographic imaging of the carotid arteries to visualize arterial lumen, flow, stenosis, and vascular abnormalities.
items.usage: Used to evaluate carotid artery stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm, dissection, and vascular malformations, especially in stroke workup and pre-intervention planning.
